learning_goal: Name the three intercostal layers in order from the surface, state the fibre direction and the breathing action of each, and say which plane the neurovascular bundle runs in.

structures.name: external intercostal muscle
structures.label: External intercostal
structures.narration: The outermost of the three. Its fibres run downwards and forwards — the direction your hands take when you slide them into your front pockets. It elevates the rib below and is the muscle of quiet inspiration.

structures.name: internal intercostal muscle
structures.label: Internal intercostal
structures.narration: The middle layer. Its fibres run at right angles to the external — downwards and backwards. Its bony part depresses the ribs in forced expiration, while its cartilage part between the costal cartilages elevates them.

structures.name: innermost intercostal muscle
structures.label: Innermost intercostal
structures.narration: The deepest and the most incomplete — it covers only the middle of each space. It matters because of the plane in front of it: the intercostal nerve and vessels run between this layer and the internal intercostal.

structures.name: right transversus thoracis
structures.label: Transversus thoracis (right)
structures.narration: A fan on the inner surface of the anterior chest wall, spreading from the back of the sternum to costal cartilages two to six. The internal thoracic artery runs across its front.

structures.name: left transversus thoracis
structures.label: Transversus thoracis (left)
structures.narration: A fan on the inner surface of the anterior chest wall, spreading from the back of the sternum to costal cartilages two to six. The internal thoracic artery runs across its front.

structures.name: right costal cartilage
structures.label: Costal cartilage (right)
structures.narration: Between the cartilages the internal intercostal continues as its interchondral part — the one part of that muscle that helps you breathe in.

structures.name: set of right levatores costarum longi
structures.label: Levatores costarum longi
structures.narration: Small fan-shaped muscles running from the transverse processes down to the rib below — the breves to the next rib, the longi skipping one. They elevate the ribs and are why the back of the wall is thicker than a front-on view suggests. Dorsal rami, not intercostal nerves.

structures.name: set of right levatores costarum breves
structures.label: Levatores costarum breves
structures.narration: Small fan-shaped muscles running from the transverse processes down to the rib below — the breves to the next rib, the longi skipping one. They elevate the ribs and are why the back of the wall is thicker than a front-on view suggests. Dorsal rami, not intercostal nerves.

views.title: See it in the body
views.narration: Eleven spaces on each side, and every one of them is filled by muscle. The ribs are only the frame; the intercostals are what turns the frame into a moving wall.

views.title: Take the ribs away
views.narration: Strip the cage and the muscle sheets remain as a continuous wall from the vertebrae behind to the sternum in front. That continuity is what makes the thorax airtight enough to hold a negative pressure.

views.title: Three layers, outside in
views.narration: External, internal, innermost — the same order as the three flat muscles of the abdominal wall, because they are the same sheet carried up into the chest.

views.title: Which way do the fibres run
views.narration: External fibres run downwards and forwards — hands in your pockets. Internal fibres cross them at a right angle, downwards and backwards. Get the direction and you can name the layer on any specimen.

views.title: Breathing in
views.narration: The external intercostals pull each rib up towards the one above. Every rib rises a little, the cage widens and deepens, pressure inside falls, and air follows it in. In quiet breathing they work alongside the diaphragm and nothing else is needed.

views.title: Forcing air out
views.narration: Quiet expiration is passive — the wall simply recoils. When you cough, shout or blow hard, the bony part of the internal intercostals pulls the ribs down and the abdominal muscles push from below.

views.title: The plane that matters clinically
views.narration: Between the internal and the innermost layer lies the neurovascular plane, and the vein, artery and nerve sit tucked under the lower border of the rib above. So a needle or a chest drain goes in just above the lower rib of the space, never below the upper one.

views.title: The wall seen from inside
views.narration: Transversus thoracis is only visible from inside the chest. It fans from the back of the sternum onto the costal cartilages, and the internal thoracic artery crosses in front of it before dividing into the superior epigastric and musculophrenic arteries.

gaps: Each intercostal layer is one model covering all the spaces at once, not eleven separate muscles, so a single space cannot be isolated. The teaching that depends on one space — the neurovascular plane, drain insertion — is carried by the cross-section beat and the narration instead.

The external and internal intercostal membranes have no models. The external muscle is replaced in front by a membrane and the internal behind by another; both are named in narration only, and a student cannot see where each sheet stops.

Subcostal muscles are not in the catalog and are not shown. Levatores costarum ARE — FMA74075 and FMA74077 on the right, FMA74076 and FMA74078 on the left, as longi and breves sets — and an earlier note here wrongly said otherwise, which is why the posterior part of the wall looks thinner than it is. They should be added.

The intercostal nerve, artery and vein are not present. Only the plane they occupy can be shown, so this scene does NOT cover the curriculum structure "Intercostal neurovascular bundle" — that needs its own scene, and the VAN order still has to be taught there.

Fibre direction is the single most examinable fact here and it is narrated rather than shown, because no op draws fibre orientation. A diagram-mode companion would carry it better; diagram is recorded as the deferred mode.
